picks.title: S1E15 — Bringing Ganga to Earth | Ramayan – The Eternal Journey
picks.summary: Bhagiratha takes on a sacred mission: to bring the divine river Ganga down to Earth and liberate the sons of Sagara.Through years of intense austerity, Bhagiratha earns the blessings of Brahma and Shiva. But Ganga’s descent is so powerful that only Shiva can receive her safely. From Shiva’s matted locks, the river finally reaches the Earth and follows Bhagiratha toward the ashes of his ancestors.In this episode of Ramayan – The Eternal Journey, discover the devotion, perseverance, and divine intervention behind one of the Ramayan’s most enduring stories — the descent of Ganga.Presented by Drea
picks.reason: Narrates Bhagiratha's sacred mission in Ramayana with themes of devotion and liberation.

picks.title: 1819: Daring to Fly Higher | Jonathan Livingston Seagull and the Ascent to Bhakti
picks.summary: In the 1970s the book Jonathan Livingston Seagull became a bestseller. A parable about a gull who refuses to follow the flock and discovers that his true nature is limitless. It serves as an insightful description of the spiritual path. The masses mistake worldly objects for sources of happiness — and spend their lives chasing what can never deliver. And some brave few dare to fly higher, brushing aside the disapproval of the flock. In this episode Raghunath and Kaustubha explore that courage alongside Akrūra's extraordinary prayers — about chasing the mirage and missing the divine love in one
picks.reason: Discusses spiritual path and bhakti using a parable, relating to Hindu devotional themes.

picks.title: 1816: Krishna, Vishnu and the Mystery of the Avatars
picks.summary: Most Vedic literature speaks from a perspective within this universe. But some reveal that this universe is just a tiny bubble among countless others — and invite us to view our place in existence from outside. Depending on which angle we look from, either Vishnu or Krishna will appear to be the origin of the Avatars. Raghunath and Kaustubha explore that question alongside Akrūra's extraordinary vision in the Yamuna — seeing Vishnu in the water, coming out to find Krishna on the chariot, going back in and seeing Vishnu again. When I am seeing you, what have I not seen? Srimad Bhagavatam 10.39.
picks.reason: Explores Vishnu and Krishna avatars and cosmic perspective from Vedic literature.
